newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar slumps on current account, MCI minus 70.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar slumps on current account, MCI minus 70.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar dropped in response to a larger-than-expected March quarter current account deficit on Friday in a response that analysts said reflected the market's desire to push for another easing in monetary conditions.

The kiwi slipped to 0.6709/16 against the U.S. unit, from just over 0.6720 before the data at 2245 GMT, and the Monetary Conditions Index, which measures how much market conditions diverge from the Reserve Bank's ideal mix, indicated about 756 points, or 68 basis points below the RB's preferred level.
The bank has said it prefers conditions to stay within 50 b.p. of its central line.
The March quarter deficit came in at NZ$723 million, compared with an average market expectation of $212.2 million.
Forecasts had ranged from a surplus of $100 million to a deficit of $450 million.
